messages.content: Refactor the auth module: split session handling out of src/auth/index.ts, then move token refresh into its own service. Keep the public API the same.

Plan: 1) extract session handling into src/auth/session.ts, 2) move token refresh into src/services/token.ts, 3) update imports and keep src/auth/index.ts re-exporting the same public functions, 4) run the full test suite. Step 1 is done: session create, validate, and destroy now live in src/auth/session.ts, and index.ts re-exports them. npm test: 208 passed, 0 failed.
Good. Is there anything risky in step 2?

The main risk is the refresh timer. It reads the session store directly, so moving it creates a circular import between session.ts and token.ts unless the store is passed in; I plan to inject the store into the token service. Concurrent refreshes are the other risk: two requests can trigger a refresh at once, so the service should share one in-flight promise.
Also, auth/refresh.spec.ts was flaky yesterday. Anything to know?
It uses real timers with a 50 ms margin, so it fails intermittently on slow CI runners. Switching it to fake timers would make it deterministic. I have not changed it yet.

I did step 2 myself: token refresh is now in src/services/token.ts with the store injected and a shared in-flight promise. I also switched refresh.spec.ts to fake timers. npm test: 212 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. No staging deploy yet. Give me a status update based only on what I just told you.
